{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring Security with Java configuration and externalized application properties or YAML configuration.",
    "Support file-based authentication through configurable users, password encoders, and roles, with HTTP authentication applied to all existing application endpoints by default.",
    "Support LDAP authentication as an alternative security provider, configurable through LDAP URL, base DN, bind credentials, user search, group search, and role mapping.",
    "Make file-based and LDAP security modes mutually exclusive through an explicit security-mode configuration, while allowing security to be disabled for local development and tests.",
    "Implement default role-based access control with Admin and Viewer roles, using a deny-by-default policy for protected endpoints and configurable endpoint authorization rules.",
    "Implement the Kerberized HDFS sink using Hadoop security configuration, principal, keytab, and delegation to the Hadoop FileSystem APIs; credentials are supplied through external configuration rather than embedded in code.",
    "For database mass-ingestion, perform the requested integration spike and produce a design specification comparing JDBC, native database clients, bulk-export tools, CDC, and batch ingestion options; implementation is excluded from this increment.",
    "Implement the HBase sink using the HBase client API with configurable quorum, namespace, table, row-key, column-family, qualifier, batching, and retry behavior.",
    "Implement the File Roll sink using configurable local directory, filename pattern, rollover size or time policy, append behavior, encoding, and flush behavior.",
    "Implement the JMX source using Spring Integration JMX support to subscribe to notifications from configured MBeans and publish normalized messages into the application messaging flow.",
    "Preserve existing endpoint and message contracts where possible, and expose new functionality through configuration rather than introducing application-specific APIs.",
    "Add unit, integration, security, and connector tests using mocks and embedded or containerized test dependencies where practical."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "An existing Spring-based application, build, deployment structure, and endpoint inventory are available; this estimate does not include creating the application from scratch.",
    "The project will target Java 17 or later and a Spring Framework/Spring Boot version compatible with the stated requirement.",
    "One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work effort, not elapsed calendar time.",
    "The existing endpoints can be protected through a shared Spring Security filter chain without redesigning endpoint business logic.",
    "File-based security means application-managed users and roles supplied through external configuration or a local credential file; no administrative user-management UI is required.",
    "LDAP infrastructure, certificates, test directory data, and connection details will be available for integration testing, or representative test doubles will be used.",
    "Kerberos realm, principals, keytabs, Hadoop libraries, and a testable HDFS environment are available from the target platform team; setting up production Hadoop or Kerberos infrastructure is excluded.",
    "The Kerberized HDFS sink extends or integrates with an existing sink framework and does not require redesigning the entire event-processing pipeline.",
    "The HBase sink targets a compatible HBase client version and an available HBase test environment; schema-management tooling and large-scale performance tuning are excluded.",
    "The File Roll sink writes to a filesystem accessible to the application process; distributed filesystem semantics, external log shipping, and multi-node coordination are excluded.",
    "The JMX source only requires notification subscription and message publication; a separate JMX management console or arbitrary MBean mutation API is not required.",
    "The database mass-ingestion story is limited to the specified spike, integration-option analysis, collaborative design, and documentation; production ingestion code is not part of this estimate.",
    "Normal code review, security review, and acceptance feedback are represented within the testing, documentation, and final acceptance activities rather than as separate parallel resources."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Baseline discovery and endpoint/extension inventory",
      "activity_description": "Review the existing repository, build, endpoint mappings, message flows, sink/source extension points, configuration conventions, and current test coverage. Identify compatibility constraints and create an implementation checklist for U1-U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Cross-cutting architecture and configuration design",
      "activity_description": "Define configuration properties, profiles, dependency changes, security-mode selection, connector lifecycle, error handling, retry behavior, observability, and backward-compatibility rules for the increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "File-based security implementation",
      "activity_description": "Add configurable file or property-backed users, password encoding, authentication handling, security filter-chain configuration, protected endpoint defaults, and local-development configuration for U1.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "LDAP security implementation",
      "activity_description": "Add LDAP provider configuration, connection and bind settings, user and group searches, role mapping, TLS-related configuration hooks, startup validation, and operational error handling for U2.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Admin and Viewer access-control implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement default authorization rules for Admin and Viewer roles, configurable endpoint overrides, deny-by-default behavior for protected routes, and authorization failure responses for U3.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Kerberized HDFS sink",
      "activity_description": "Implement or extend the HDFS sink to authenticate with Kerberos using principal and keytab configuration, create and reuse secure filesystem clients, write events, handle rollover or flush integration, and provide actionable failures for U4.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Database mass-ingestion integration spike",
      "activity_description": "Investigate JDBC and non-JDBC integration options, bulk export and CDC alternatives, operational constraints, supported database categories, security implications, and scalability trade-offs. Collaborate on the recommended design and document the outcome for U5.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "HBase sink",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable HBase connectivity, table and schema mapping, row-key and cell mapping, batching, retries, connection lifecycle, error handling, and sink integration for U6.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "File Roll sink",
      "activity_description": "Implement local filesystem event writing with configurable directory, naming pattern, encoding, append behavior, time or size rollover, flush and close handling, and failure recovery for U7.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "JMX source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable JMX connector and MBean notification subscription, notification filtering, message conversion, reconnect and lifecycle handling, and publication into the existing source pipeline for U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Security unit and integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Add tests for file authentication, LDAP authentication using a test directory or test double, role authorization, protected endpoint coverage, disabled-security mode, invalid configuration, and authentication/authorization failures.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Connector and source/sink testing",
      "activity_description": "Add unit and integration tests for Kerberos configuration handling, HDFS writes, HBase writes, file rollover, JMX notification delivery, retries, resource cleanup, malformed events, and connector failure paths.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Configuration documentation and examples",
      "activity_description": "Document security modes, Admin and Viewer authorization, LDAP setup, Kerberos and HDFS configuration, HBase and File Roll properties, JMX source usage, limitations, deployment prerequisites, and the database spike recommendation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A14",
      "activity_name": "Build, packaging, static quality, and compatibility updates",
      "activity_description": "Update dependencies and build files, verify packaging and startup behavior, add sample configurations, run static checks, resolve compatibility issues, and ensure new modules can be enabled independently.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A15",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end verification and acceptance support",
      "activity_description": "Execute representative secured endpoint, HDFS, HBase, File Roll, and JMX scenarios; address integration defects; perform regression checks; and prepare the increment for acceptance.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 98
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Security with Java configuration and externalized application properties or YAML configuration.
Support file-based authentication through configurable users, password encoders, and roles, with HTTP authentication applied to all existing application endpoints by default.
Support LDAP authentication as an alternative security provider, configurable through LDAP URL, base DN, bind credentials, user search, group search, and role mapping.
Make file-based and LDAP security modes mutually exclusive through an explicit security-mode configuration, while allowing security to be disabled for local development and tests.
Implement default role-based access control with Admin and Viewer roles, using a deny-by-default policy for protected endpoints and configurable endpoint authorization rules.

Implement the Kerberized HDFS sink using Hadoop security configuration, principal, keytab, and delegation to the Hadoop FileSystem APIs; credentials are supplied through external configuration rather than embedded in code.

For database mass-ingestion, perform the requested integration spike and produce a design specification comparing JDBC, native database clients, bulk-export tools, CDC, and batch ingestion options; implementation is excluded from this increment.
Implement the HBase sink using the HBase client API with configurable quorum, namespace, table, row-key, column-family, qualifier, batching, and retry behavior.
Implement the File Roll sink using configurable local directory, filename pattern, rollover size or time policy, append behavior, encoding, and flush behavior.
Implement the JMX source using Spring Integration JMX support to subscribe to notifications from configured MBeans and publish normalized messages into the application messaging flow.
Preserve existing endpoint and message contracts where possible, and expose new functionality through configuration rather than introducing application-specific APIs.
Add unit, integration, security, and connector tests using mocks and embedded or containerized test dependencies where practical.
assumptions: An existing Spring-based application, build, deployment structure, and endpoint inventory are available; this estimate does not include creating the application from scratch.
The project will target Java 17 or later and a Spring Framework/Spring Boot version compatible with the stated requirement.
One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work effort, not elapsed calendar time.
The existing endpoints can be protected through a shared Spring Security filter chain without redesigning endpoint business logic.
File-based security means application-managed users and roles supplied through external configuration or a local credential file; no administrative user-management UI is required.
LDAP infrastructure, certificates, test directory data, and connection details will be available for integration testing, or representative test doubles will be used.

Kerberos realm, principals, keytabs, Hadoop libraries, and a testable HDFS environment are available from the target platform team; setting up production Hadoop or Kerberos infrastructure is excluded.
The Kerberized HDFS sink extends or integrates with an existing sink framework and does not require redesigning the entire event-processing pipeline.
The HBase sink targets a compatible HBase client version and an available HBase test environment; schema-management tooling and large-scale performance tuning are excluded.
The File Roll sink writes to a filesystem accessible to the application process; distributed filesystem semantics, external log shipping, and multi-node coordination are excluded.
The JMX source only requires notification subscription and message publication; a separate JMX management console or arbitrary MBean mutation API is not required.
The database mass-ingestion story is limited to the specified spike, integration-option analysis, collaborative design, and documentation; production ingestion code is not part of this estimate.
Normal code review, security review, and acceptance feedback are represented within the testing, documentation, and final acceptance activities rather than as separate parallel resources.

activities.activity_description: Review the existing repository, build, endpoint mappings, message flows, sink/source extension points, configuration conventions, and current test coverage. Identify compatibility constraints and create an implementation checklist for U1-U8.

Define configuration properties, profiles, dependency changes, security-mode selection, connector lifecycle, error handling, retry behavior, observability, and backward-compatibility rules for the increment.

Add configurable file or property-backed users, password encoding, authentication handling, security filter-chain configuration, protected endpoint defaults, and local-development configuration for U1.
Add LDAP provider configuration, connection and bind settings, user and group searches, role mapping, TLS-related configuration hooks, startup validation, and operational error handling for U2.
Implement default authorization rules for Admin and Viewer roles, configurable endpoint overrides, deny-by-default behavior for protected routes, and authorization failure responses for U3.

Implement or extend the HDFS sink to authenticate with Kerberos using principal and keytab configuration, create and reuse secure filesystem clients, write events, handle rollover or flush integration, and provide actionable failures for U4.

Investigate JDBC and non-JDBC integration options, bulk export and CDC alternatives, operational constraints, supported database categories, security implications, and scalability trade-offs. Collaborate on the recommended design and document the outcome for U5.
Implement configurable HBase connectivity, table and schema mapping, row-key and cell mapping, batching, retries, connection lifecycle, error handling, and sink integration for U6.
Implement local filesystem event writing with configurable directory, naming pattern, encoding, append behavior, time or size rollover, flush and close handling, and failure recovery for U7.

Implement configurable JMX connector and MBean notification subscription, notification filtering, message conversion, reconnect and lifecycle handling, and publication into the existing source pipeline for U8.

Add tests for file authentication, LDAP authentication using a test directory or test double, role authorization, protected endpoint coverage, disabled-security mode, invalid configuration, and authentication/authorization failures.

Add unit and integration tests for Kerberos configuration handling, HDFS writes, HBase writes, file rollover, JMX notification delivery, retries, resource cleanup, malformed events, and connector failure paths.

Document security modes, Admin and Viewer authorization, LDAP setup, Kerberos and HDFS configuration, HBase and File Roll properties, JMX source usage, limitations, deployment prerequisites, and the database spike recommendation.

activities.activity_description: Update dependencies and build files, verify packaging and startup behavior, add sample configurations, run static checks, resolve compatibility issues, and ensure new modules can be enabled independently.
Execute representative secured endpoint, HDFS, HBase, File Roll, and JMX scenarios; address integration defects; perform regression checks; and prepare the increment for acceptance.
